solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Branch backing bank’s closure (4)

indicatorNotes.closure: a closure is where something ends, so the last letter of 'bank'

blocks.note: backing = FOR, as in being for a plan

annotation.surface: A branch office stays open while the parent bank is shut down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like a reversal instruction, but here it simply means support: FOR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: where a road or river splits, each arm is a branch.

entries.clue: Is afraid to pin article down (8)

indicatorNotes.to pin: FEARS pins THE, holding it in place inside

annotation.surface: Someone fears pinning an item down, as if nervous of a wrestling move.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Down' reads as part of the phrase 'pin down', but it is the definition: the soft feathers of a bird.
annotation.definitionFit: Down is the fine soft covering of feathers on a bird.

entries.clue: Legal tender? (10,5)

blocks.note: legal read as officially on the register, not as lawful money
a tender is one who tends the sick, not currency

annotation.surface: A question about money: what counts as legal tender?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Legal tender' means currency, but read it as a tender (one who tends the sick) who is legal, that is, officially registered.
annotation.definitionFit: A registered nurse is a qualified carer whose name is on the official register.

entries.clue: Footnote about each nose that may be blown (10)

blocks.note: PS, postscript, a note at the foot of a letter
EA is the standard abbreviation for each
hooter is British slang for a nose

annotation.surface: A footnote about noses that can be blown, like a comic appendix to an anatomy text.
annotation.walkthrough: The nose looks like the thing that may be blown; in fact the definition is the peashooter, a tube you blow peas through.
annotation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a toy tube that fires peas when you blow into it.

entries.clue: Are sons opening door? (5)

indicatorNotes.opening: S opens the door by going into it

annotation.surface: A question: is it the sons who are opening the door?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like the start of a question; it is the definition, the verb 'to be' in the plural.
annotation.definitionFit: 'They are' and 'they exist' say the same thing.

entries.clue: Doctor to get dairy products delivered (3,6)

indicatorNotes.delivered: a speech is delivered, so the words are spoken

blocks.note: get = see, as in 'I get it'

annotation.surface: A doctor orders cheeses and yoghurts to the door.
annotation.walkthrough: The Fremantle Doctor is the cooling afternoon sea breeze in Western Australia, which is why 'Doctor' is fair.
annotation.definitionFit: Several cooling coastal winds are nicknamed 'the Doctor', most famously the Fremantle Doctor in Perth.

entries.clue: Cato upset by Antony’s wife (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: the letters of CATO are knocked over into a new order

blocks.note: the four letters of CATO rearranged

annotation.surface: The Roman statesman Cato is upset by Mark Antony's wife, a scene from Roman politics.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word sits in Rome, so 'by' reads as agency; it is simply VIA.
annotation.definitionFit: Octavia, sister of Octavian, married Mark Antony.

entries.clue: Ground troops? (11,4)

blocks.note: ground read as land held, territory, not the battlefield floor

annotation.surface: A plain military term: soldiers who fight on land.
annotation.walkthrough: Ground troops are infantry; read 'ground' as territory and you reach the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force.
annotation.definitionFit: The Territorial Army was the part-time reserve of the British Army.

entries.clue: Military commander invading from Melbourne (6)

indicatorNotes.invading: the answer has invaded the words, sitting inside them

annotation.surface: A general invades from Melbourne, an Australian attack.
annotation.walkthrough: Erwin Rommel was the German field marshal known as the Desert Fox.
annotation.definitionFit: Rommel commanded German forces in North Africa in the Second World War.

entries.clue: Disrepute among footballers — gosh! (6)

blocks.note: the FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'gosh!'

annotation.surface: Shock at the disgrace among footballers, like a tabloid headline.
annotation.walkthrough: The Football Association runs English football, so the clue lets its initials stand for footballers in general.
annotation.definitionFit: Infamy is a bad reputation, public disgrace.

entries.clue: Country squire in harbour, but heading off (9)

indicatorNotes.in: GENT goes in the harbour word
indicatorNotes.heading off: MARINA loses its head, the first letter

blocks.note: a squire is a gentleman, GENT

annotation.surface: A country squire is found in the harbour, but he is setting off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country squire' reads as a type of landowner; 'Country' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Argentina is one of many countries.

entries.clue: Buzz is missing from this drink (5)

indicatorNotes.is missing from: the letters IS are missing from THIS

annotation.surface: This drink has lost its buzz, a complaint about a flat cocktail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buzz is missing' reads as one phrase about a drink; 'Buzz' is the definition and 'is' is the letters taken away.
annotation.definitionFit: A thrum is a low continuous humming or buzzing sound.

entries.clue: Christmas Eve, so I shot Nipper’s picture (3,7,5)

indicatorNotes.shot: the letters are shot to pieces and reassembled

annotation.surface: On Christmas Eve I took a photograph of my young son.
annotation.walkthrough: Nipper is the dog listening to a gramophone in the painting His Master's Voice, the HMV logo; 'Nipper' passes for a child, and 'shot' for taking a photo.
annotation.definitionFit: Francis Barraud's painting of Nipper the terrier is titled His Master's Voice.

entries.clue: Mike leaves to repair piping (5)

blocks.note: to remedy is to put right
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet; it is removed

annotation.surface: Mike walks away from fixing the plumbing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piping' suggests plumbing; it is the adjective, as in a thin, high voice.
annotation.definitionFit: A reedy voice is thin and high, like a piping one.

entries.clue: Film precisely frames communist soldiers (8)

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

annotation.surface: A film shows communist soldiers in exact framing, as if describing a war movie's cinematography.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Frames' fits the film surface, but it is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Predator is the 1987 Arnold Schwarzenegger science-fiction action film.

entries.clue: Exploitative position adopted by soldier in charge (9)

indicatorNotes.adopted by: the position is taken on by the soldier, so it follows him in the answer

blocks.note: a sit is a posture, a position you take

annotation.surface: A soldier in charge takes up a position that exploits others.
annotation.walkthrough: A sit is a posture, which is how a one-word position can be so short; the soldier is the crossword's usual paratrooper.
annotation.definitionFit: Parasitic means living off others, exploitative.

entries.clue: Methane in planet has to limit gravity’s effect (5,3)

indicatorNotes.to limit: HAS limits G by enclosing it

blocks.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

annotation.surface: A scientific note: methane on a planet has to keep gravity's pull in check.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like planetary science, with 'in planet' seeming to place the methane; 'in' only joins definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Marsh gas is methane given off by rotting vegetation in marshes.

entries.clue: Inevitably, man will escape execution (8)

indicatorNotes.will escape: MAN escapes from the word, leaving it

annotation.surface: A condemned man will, inevitably, escape the gallows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Execution' suggests the gallows; it means carrying something out, a performance.
annotation.definitionFit: Perforce is a formal word for necessarily, inevitably.

entries.clue: Message about posh old man’s indiscretion (4,3)

blocks.note: pa is father, the old man; PA'S

annotation.surface: A message about a posh father's social blunder.
annotation.walkthrough: U for upper class comes from the old 'U and non-U' distinction in British speech.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: faux pas, French for false step, names an indiscreet social slip.

entries.clue: Perhaps one’s best friend (5)

blocks.note: one's best crockery, the good plates kept for guests
Cockney rhyming slang: a word rhyming with plate stands for mate

annotation.surface: A remark that someone may be your closest friend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Best friend' reads as one phrase; split it after 'best', which is the good crockery.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Best china' is the good crockery, and in Cockney rhyming slang a china is a mate.

entries.clue: After tea, tea dance (3-3)

blocks.note: cha is British slang for tea

annotation.surface: After afternoon tea comes a tea dance, a genteel social occasion.
annotation.walkthrough: A tea dance is an afternoon dance, so 'tea dance' reads as one thing; split it.
annotation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance.

entries.clue: Border community area in windy S Pole (2,4)

indicatorNotes.in: A goes in with the other letters

annotation.surface: A settlement in a windy area at the South Pole.
annotation.walkthrough: El Paso is the Texas city on the US border with Mexico.
annotation.definitionFit: El Paso sits right on the Mexican border, facing Ciudad Juárez.

entries.clue: Collection of delivery systems? Actual listing is wrong (10,5)

indicatorNotes.wrong: the letters are put wrong, into a new order

annotation.surface: A complaint that a catalogue of parcel services has mistakes.
annotation.walkthrough: Languages and dialects are the 'delivery systems' of speech; a linguistic atlas maps them, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A linguistic atlas is a set of maps showing where languages and dialects are spoken.

entries.clue: Temper that is holding work up (5)

indicatorNotes.holding: IE holds the other word inside
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up turns the word backwards

blocks.note: run = work, as a machine runs

annotation.surface: A bad temper is what is holding up the work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Temper' reads as anger, but it is the verb: to toughen, as steel is tempered.
annotation.definitionFit: To inure someone is to harden them, as tempering hardens metal.

entries.clue: Just out of bed. A bunk? Not quite (5)

indicatorNotes.Not quite: TRIPE is not quite complete, losing its last letter

blocks.note: bunk = nonsense = TRIPE, less its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone has just got up, and a bunk bed has not quite been slept in.
annotation.walkthrough: The bed is the sea bed: an anchor is atrip when it has just been pulled clear of the bottom. 'Bunk' suggests a bed but means nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: Atrip is a nautical term for an anchor just lifted off the sea bed.

entries.clue: Lies low after taking this? (5,4)

blocks.note: the surface sense is hiding away; the meant sense is that lies become few
the thing taken that stops the lying

annotation.surface: Someone takes something and then lies low, hiding away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lies low' means hiding; read it instead as the number of lies falling after the drug is taken.
annotation.definitionFit: A truth drug is supposed to make people stop lying.

entries.clue: In one respect possibly common knowledge (4,6)

indicatorNotes.possibly: the letters could possibly be arranged another way

annotation.surface: A hedge: in one respect, this might be something everyone knows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In one respect' reads as a set phrase; 'In' is only a link and the fodder starts at 'one'.
annotation.definitionFit: An open secret is something supposedly secret that everyone knows.

entries.clue: Affirmative votes, or just one (4)

blocks.note: the parliamentary word for votes in favour
split the same letters after the first and they spell a single vote in favour

annotation.surface: A note on a count of yes votes, or a lone one.
annotation.walkthrough: AYES are yes votes in Parliament; read it as A YES and it is just one yes vote.
annotation.definitionFit: A parliamentary term: MPs voting in favour call out 'aye', and the tally is the ayes.
